summary: This work presents robust cavity metrology observables based on the scissors phase $\Sigma = 2\phi_0 - (\phi_- + \phi_+)$ that eliminate systematic errors in Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) spectroscopy caused by sideband amplitude imbalance and demodulation-phase errors. An experimentally efficient observable $\mathbb{S}_Q = E_- E_+ E_0^2 \sin\Sigma$ is introduced that requires only addition and multiplication (no arctangent) and is demonstrated in both optical cavity locking and superconducting qubit readout.
motivation: PDH spectroscopy is widely used for precision cavity measurements across quantum technologies, but suffers from systematic zero-crossing offsets due to residual amplitude modulation and demodulation-phase errors, which limit the performance of ultrastable lasers and scalable quantum computers.
method: The three-tone interrogation signal is decomposed into orthogonal collective phase modes ($\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$, $\Sigma$), and heterodyne detection of all three tones is used to reconstruct the scissors phase $\Sigma$ and the computationally efficient observable $\mathbb{S}_Q$ directly from measured IQ quadratures, rejecting common-mode and differential-mode phase errors by construction.
result: In optical spectroscopy with 17% sideband imbalance and varying demodulation phase, $\mathbb{S}_Q$ maintains a stable zero-crossing while PDH shows demodulation-dependent offsets proportional to $\beta\Delta_{\text{amp}}$; in microwave qubit readout under RF timing errors inducing both $\alpha$ and $\beta$, $\mathbb{S}_Q$ retains 95% Gaussian resolvability compared to PDH's 50% under the same degraded conditions.
